description: We're a small team of people who love tech, space, and coming up with random ideas that somehow turn into projects. We're into coding, AI, game development and design, and always up for learning something new. Looking for people who enjoy building things, experimenting, and thinking outside the box. Bonus points if you're a space nerd too. 🚀
summary:
POLARIS: Ice Hunter Mars is a space mission simulation game developed by Team astronaut.exe. We wanted to create an experience that gives people a better idea of what actually goes into planning and carrying out a mission to Mars, to collect water ice samples and bring them safely back to Earth.

The challenge was to build a game where players could design, manage and simulate a complete space mission while dealing with real-world constraints. We approached this by creating an interactive experience that brings together mission planning, landing-site selection, resource management, astronaut survival and communication with Earth.

Rather than simply explaining these concepts, we wanted players to experience the decisions involved and understand how one choice can affect an entire mission. POLARIS is our way of making space exploration more accessible, engaging and fun to learn about.
details:
POLARIS: Ice Hunter Mars is a 3D interactive space mission simulation developed by Team astronaut.exe. The idea was to let players experience what goes into planning and carrying out a mission to Mars, with the objective of collecting water ice samples and bringing them safely back to Earth.

The game takes players through different stages of a mission, starting with choosing a landing site and mission profile, followed by preparing the spacecraft and managing its systems. Players have to monitor oxygen, temperature, astronaut health and other life-support systems, maintain communication with Earth, and eventually collect and verify their ice samples. We also included different Martian landing locations, each with its own challenges and potential for ice collection.

One of the main things we considered was how real mission decisions are interconnected. Choosing a landing site affects resource requirements, while equipment choices involve balancing mass, power and budget. We also wanted to include aspects that are often overlooked, such as astronaut wellbeing, communication failures and sample preservation.

We developed POLARIS as a browser-based project using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with a 3D game environment, interactive interfaces and mission control systems. The project is hosted on Netlify.

What makes POLARIS different is that we didn't want it to be just another space exploration game. We wanted players to understand the planning and responsibility behind an actual mission. By combining research, engineering concepts and interactive gameplay, we hope to make space mission design more approachable and encourage people to explore the science behind space exploration.
